Duplicate Blue Buff and Adaptive Helm multiplier aggregation.
Lifeline burst protection and incoming Titan stacks for exposed carries.

nonItemChangeExplanation.reason: The flat and max-health trail shares now settle as one native periodic hit independently of equipped items, preserving one hit opportunity for recipient items such as Titan's Resolve. Combining those terms changes floating-point operation order.
nonItemChangeExplanation.elderDragonExplanation: Ignite now carries its unit spell applicability and ability-crit status; bare Elder builds lack Precision and remain bit-identical.

verification.note: Original probes expose the pre-fix model and are retained as history. Focused regression, all TFT Python tests including full preserved-input goldens, and Rust tests passed on the recorded corrected model. Active 18.4b leaderboard refresh remains in progress; static evidence and model checks do not certify live-client equivalence.

liveDashboardUi.alsoChecked: Live low-trait leaderboard and Sivir cell passed the same damage UI harness.

leaderboardImpact.limit: This selection-specific comparison is not a measure of changes in all scenarios or win rate.

benchmarkAssumptions: All four configured frontliners have Tank role. Giant Slayer therefore receives its conditional bonus against all four; a Fighter frontliner would not qualify. This is an enemy-board choice, separate from the item source-gate bug.
Permanent30% Sunder and Shred are supplied by the team. Redundant reductions must not be counted twice when fixing item refresh events.
Protected carries receive no damage; defensive and ally-healing utility cannot be treated as demonstrated damage advantages for those holders.

source.additionalModifiers: Each attribute also gets AddFinal(-ADAPMultiplier) and AddFinal(+1), preserving the baseline.

findings.expected: Copy multiplier 1 + count * (1.1 - 1), applied to gained AD/AP, including its own ordinary stats.
findings.observed: Fx.apply_item multiplies 1.1 once per copy.
findings.notes: Single-copy bonus-only scope agrees with the native AddFinal cancellation. Duplicate stacking is the error.
findings.resolutionDescription: Duplicate Blue Buff bonuses now add their extra percentages: 1 + 0.10 * copies. The multiplier still applies to gained AD/AP, including item and trait bonuses, while preserving base AD and base 100 AP.

findings.expected: Incoming mana multiplier 1 + count * (1.15 - 1).
findings.observed: Fx.apply_item compounds 1.15 once per copy.
findings.notes: Single-copy mana, mana regeneration, MR and role bonuses match. This can alter cast thresholds for duplicate Helm builds.
findings.resolutionDescription: Duplicate Adaptive Helm bonuses now use incoming mana multiplier 1 + 0.15 * copies. Per-copy ordinary stats and mana regeneration are retained; regression arithmetic covers attack mana and regeneration.

findings.expected: Ionic Spark does not receive Giant Slayer conditional tank amp.
findings.observed: Fight.amp adds amp_vs_tank for any tank target; PLAIN Ionic Spark damage takes that amp.
findings.notes: Do not classify all damage solely by item name: native Bramble Vest damage has Damage.Source.Unit. This finding establishes Ionic Spark, with other sources requiring their own native tags.
findings.resolutionDescription: Conditional tank amplification now requires Unit-sourced damage. Item-sourced Ionic Spark and Trait damage are excluded; native Unit-sourced Bramble retaliation remains eligible independently of its absent attack/spell applicability tags.

findings.issue: Attack-speed growth incorrectly stops at immunity expiry
findings.native: GA_Quicksilver RepeatAction(StackFrequency,99), separate infinite stacking AS GE; EffectDuration belongs to separate immunity GE.
findings.observed: One copy asStack=.54 at18.01/19.01/25.01s; stacking no longer grows.
findings.expected: Stacking timer continues past18s; +3% per additional second. Exact inherited cap/default and initial RepeatAction offset not established.
findings.correction: Separate AS timer lifetime from ccImmuneDuration; preserve additive copy contributions unless native cap semantics prove otherwise.
findings.resolutionDescription: Quicksilver attack-speed growth now continues for the fight rather than stopping at the separate 18-second CC-immunity deadline. Additive copy contributions and the existing one-second accumulation policy are retained.

findings.issue: Critical attack mana credited once per attack frame, not per eligible critical damage hit
findings.native: GA_NashorsTooth requires WasCrit+AppliesOnAttack, PostApply applies2mana. Elder Dragon's splash GE has AppliesOnAttack+RollAlways.
findings.observed: One unlocked ElderDragon attack: three positive guaranteed crit hits, one copy14mana, two copies18mana.
findings.expected: Fighter10+base2+threecritbonuses2=18mana foronecopy; Fighter10+base4+threecritbonuses4=26mana fortwocopies.
findings.correction: Keep baseManaPerAttack on attack; award the critical increment after each accepted AppliesOnAttack damage event. Plain spell crits are ineligible. Mana-locked channels require separate policy evidence.
findings.resolutionDescription: Nashor critical mana now arrives after each accepted critical hit carrying attack applicability, once per eligible target and item copy. Base attack mana remains on the attack event. Plain spell crits and rejected zero-damage hits cannot grant the critical increment; existing mana-lock acceptance policy is retained.

findings.issue: All positive incoming damage grants stacks, ignoring native attack/spell applicability filter
findings.native: PostApply counter requires HasAnyTags(AppliesOnAttack,AppliesOnSpell); Bramble retaliation explicitly has DamageTags[].
findings.observed: AD100, one2%Titan, ownautos at0/1/2:102/106/108 with30thorns at0/2.
findings.expected: 102/104/106: the untagged item retaliation must not add offensive stacks.
findings.correction: Carry native applicability metadata into incoming damage and count only eligible accepted events.
findings.resolutionDescription: Titan incoming stacks now require an accepted attack- or spell-applicable damage event. Untagged Bramble retaliation and item burn do not grant incoming stacks; ordinary attack and spell damage remain eligible.

findings.issue: Incoming spell DoT integration slices counted as gameplay stack events
findings.native: Cassio poison has AppliesOnSpell and0.5s nativePeriod; initial periodic execution is not explicitly serialized.
findings.observed: 2s poison creates8 quarter-second take packets; after4ownautos finalauto3s=124 (12Titanstacks).
findings.expected: At most5logicalpoison events evenwithinitialapplication: finalauto <=118 (9stacks), or116 if firstperiod delayed.
findings.correction: Keep damage integration but separate incoming proc opportunities using source-bound native periods; do not invent extra hit opportunities or first-tick behavior.
findings.resolutionDescription: Incoming periodic stack opportunities now follow source-bound native periods, independently of the holder's items. Quarter-second damage integration does not create extra gameplay hits. Compound Ashe trail terms settle as one accepted periodic hit, including lethal hits; unknown periods create no extra proc opportunities.

findings.summary: First lethal hit does not receive the native pre-apply shield.
findings.expected: Native GA Bloodthirster has a normal PostApply threshold callback and a separate PreApply fallback: if Health+Shield−Damage <=0 and not yet procced, apply the shield before the hit.
findings.observed: Engine consumes existing shields and subtracts all damage from health first, then health_triggers creates the new shield; a killed unit dies without that shield absorbing any of the triggering hit.
limits: Normal PostApply callback timing is not inferred from the callback label alone. The reported mismatch is the explicit PreApply lethal fallback.
findings.resolutionDescription: Bloodthirster now applies its unfired lifeline shield before an otherwise lethal hit consumes health and shields. Existing shields participate in the lethal check, copies recheck after earlier applications, and the fallback can fire only once.

findings.summary: First lethal hit does not receive the native pre-apply shield.
findings.expected: Native GA ProtectorsVow has a normal PostApply threshold callback and a separate PreApply fallback: if Health+Shield−Damage <=0 and not yet procced, apply the shield before the hit.
findings.observed: Engine consumes existing shields and subtracts all damage from health first, then health_triggers creates the new shield; a killed unit dies without that shield absorbing any of the triggering hit.
limits: Normal PostApply callback timing is not inferred from the callback label alone. The reported mismatch is the explicit PreApply lethal fallback.
findings.resolutionDescription: Protector's Vow now applies its shield and paired mana grant in the otherwise-lethal pre-hit fallback. Both are spent once; shield consumption and real-encounter damage credit include the newly applied shield.

findings.summary: First lethal hit does not receive the native pre-apply shield.
findings.expected: Native GA SteraksGage has a normal PostApply threshold callback and a separate PreApply fallback: if Health+Shield−Damage <=0 and not yet procced, apply the shield before the hit.
findings.observed: Engine consumes existing shields and subtracts all damage from health first, then health_triggers creates the new shield; a killed unit dies without that shield absorbing any of the triggering hit.
limits: Normal PostApply callback timing is not inferred from the callback label alone. The reported mismatch is the explicit PreApply lethal fallback.
findings.resolutionDescription: Sterak now applies its unfired lifeline shield before an otherwise lethal hit. Native pre-hit order is modeled alongside normal threshold behavior, existing-shield checks and one-use fallback ownership.

findings.summary: Shield decay starts on the global clock instead of the effect application clock.
findings.expected: Native GE_SteraksGage_Proc has Period=.25, bExecutePeriodicEffectOnApplication=false, and ShieldApplication.bDecayOverDurationForPeriodicEffect=true: application at1.1s has no periodic decay until1.35s; shield remains520 at1.25s.
findings.observed: Engine global tick1.25 immediately removes .25s worth of decay: 520 becomes487.5.
limits: This is a phase/cadence mismatch; the evidence does not independently verify the C++ periodic shield consumer’s exact post-first-tick decay formula.
findings.resolutionDescription: Decaying Sterak shields now track quarter-second deadlines relative to their own application time, with no decay on application. Due decay settles before intervening incoming hits; the retained linear decay formula is distinct from the verified native period and phase.

findings.summary: Burst protection omits the native minimum-health override.
findings.expected: Before damage, native GA compares Health+Shield−Damage <= HPPercentageToProcAt×HealthMax, applies GE_EdgeOfNight_MinHealthBuff, and overrides HealthMin to40% of current maxHealth. The temporary override lasts .1×UntargetableDuration (.1s here) and is removed in PostApply after the hit. A1,000HP holder’s first1,500 post-mitigation burst therefore stops at400HP; missing-HP heal afterward yields490 absent debuffs.
findings.observed: Engine subtracts1,500 from1,000, heals225 from the resulting1,500 missing health, and dies at the same timestamp; no HealthMin field/clamp exists.
limits: 490HP is arithmetic from the decoded floor/heal magnitudes, not observed live-client output; decoded native consumer invocation establishes the intended HealthMin clamp.

The HealthMin attribute consumption is native C++ and was not executed in a live client here; the confirmed omission is the explicit PreApply override path, with the surviving-HP number a decoded-configuration arithmetic expectation.
findings.resolutionDescription: Edge now clamps its triggering hit at the configured 40% maximum-health floor before post-hit healing and untargetability. Later hits cannot reuse that spent floor. Shared combat credits consumed health and shields without crediting prevented overkill.

findings.summary: A hit landing exactly at the item threshold fails to proc.
findings.expected: Native GA LessEqual comparison at statement2569 includes exactly40% health.
findings.observed: Engine uses frac<thr; controlled1,000HP→400HP hit gives no heal or untargetability.
findings.resolutionDescription: Edge threshold checks now include equality, matching the native LessEqual comparison; a hit reaching exactly 40% health triggers its one-use protection and post-hit effects.

findings.expected: Native GA statement44 calls RemoveActiveEffectsWithTags with tagDebuff; this runs through the next-tick proc continuation after applying untargetability.
findings.observed: health_triggers only calls untargetable and heal; untargetable only sets untargetable_until. It does not clear realteam stun/sleep, manaReave, timed sunder/shred, or other supported negative state.
limits: Source-confirmed omission; no realteam cleanse combat was replayed in this bounded audit. Standalone benchmark enemies do not apply incoming CC. Permanent benchmark wound/sunder/shred assumptions are not native transient gameplay effects, so their removal or immediate reapplication is a separate model decision.
findings.resolutionDescription: Edge now clears supported transient combat debuffs, including stun, sleep, mana reave, timed resistance reductions, burn and wound. Permanent standalone benchmark reductions remain assumptions. Actor clocks resume overdue work at the current time after cleanse, without rewinding combat time.

findings.summary: Missing-health regeneration is integrated every.25s instead of the item’s one-second action cadence.
findings.expected: Current tooltip says2% missingHP each second; RegenTickRate=1. Native GA evaluates RegenRateCurveRow and RepeatAction(interval,9999), applying the heal on each action.
findings.observed: Engine regenMissingPct has no interval; every TICK_S=.25 computes .02×missingHP×.25. Controlled first hit at.5s produces .9 healing at.75s, before the next native one-second action.
limits: Native propertybag parameter values are opaque in this decode; interval1 is directly supported by current curve and tooltip. The decoded GA uses RepeatAction at that configured rate.
findings.resolutionDescription: Spirit Visage missing-health healing now runs on one-second action deadlines, starting at one second, rather than on every quarter-second integration slice. Existing summed copy magnitudes and incoming-healing scaling are retained.

findings.summary: The6% max-health bonus is pooled additively despite its native compound operator.
findings.expected: GE_BrambleVest_Stats HealthMax uses MultiplyCompound(1.06). Warmog/Dragon’sClaw HealthMax use legacy Multiplicitive(=MultiplyAdditive), on the same evaluation channel. For baseHP1,000: twoBramble→1,123.6; Bramble+Warmog→(1,000+500)×1.18×1.06=1,876.2.
findings.observed: Fx pools allHpMult via hp_mult +=v−1, giving1,120 and1,860. A twoWarmog control correctly yields2,720 for both additive formulas.
limits: Confirmed against archived18.3 effect operators with matching current18.4b numerical rows; latest18.4b native executable was not decoded.
findings.resolutionDescription: Bramble's 1.06 maximum-health multiplier now compounds per copy after the additive HP modifier pool. Warmog and Dragon's Claw retain additive percent stacking; timed flat-health effects use the same compound factor in standalone and shared theory schedulers.

findings.summary: Periodic and some area damage bypass the item application or refresh callback.
findings.expected: Native listeners receive accepted Damage.Source.Unit hits. Their filter does not exclude damage over time; Morello applies in PostApply. Each eligible hit should apply or refresh its burn or resistance reduction.
findings.observed: dot_ability applies effects once when scheduling the DoT; tick/deal does not refresh them. Some secondary area hits also call deal without the item callback.
examples: One 16-second Cassio poison with no attacks: Morello burn ends at10.5s while poison continues to16.5s.
Void Staff on the same poison against100MR: per-slice damage falls from14.705882 to12.5 when Shred expires at5.5s despite continuing poison.
One Scuttlecrab dance hits targets0/1/2; Morello burn applies only to target0.
limits: Some imported effect-class constants in the source functions are unresolved; the damage-listener filters and callbacks used here are resolved.
The default leaderboard already supplies permanent30% Sunder/Shred. The expiration defect does not add a second reduction in that benchmark.
DoT first-application timing and burn integration phase need separate verification.
findings.resolutionDescription: Accepted Unit-sourced area and periodic hits now apply or refresh Morello, Last Whisper and Void Staff through the common damage callback. Logical periodic opportunities use known native periods; integration slices alone cannot refresh effects. Existing permanent 30% benchmark reductions still combine by strongest effect rather than stacking twice.

findings.summary: Red Buff shares the same incomplete damage callback as Morello.
findings.observed: In the 16-second poison probe, Red Buff burn ends at5.5s while poison continues to16.5s.
findings.expected: Its current tooltip states attacks and abilities burn targets, so continuing ability damage should refresh the burn.
limits: The original missing granted-ability import was resolved by making the known GA_RedBuff package available to the unchanged strict decoder. Clean resolved damage-listener nodes establish the filters; two imported burn/wound effect references still produce visible diagnostics.
Static mechanics are from the pinned 18.3 archive; current 18.4b values are applied separately. No matched 18.4 runtime replay was performed.
findings.resolutionDescription: Red Buff now receives accepted Unit attack- or spell-applicable area and periodic hits through the common damage callback. Its native two-listener applicability gate is represented separately from Morello's Unit-source-only gate, so untagged Bramble can trigger Morello but cannot trigger Red Buff.
originalLimits: The native GE_RedBuff granted-ability class resolves to null with a missing-import warning. The exact native listener was not established for Red Buff; this classification uses the tooltip and shared engine callback.

nativeConfirmation.nodeEvidence: The GE grant resolves to GA_RedBuff_C once the omitted known package is in the allowlist. Both listener filters and their PostApply continuations are resolved nodes; unresolved GE_Burn/GE_Wound imports do not establish their defaults.

findings.summary: Sunfire continuously refreshes the current attack target instead of using its own timer and target selection.
findings.expected: The current curve sets BurnWoundFrequency=2s. The native graph filters Debuff.Burn targets, sorts by distance and uses a looping timer; burn coverage can spread among eligible nearby enemies.
findings.observed: The engine calls burn on the current target every.25s; it drops the frequency field. Four living nearby targets remain alive for8s, but only target0 burns in the controlled probe.
limits: Three native function imports are unresolved. The timer and Burn-tag filter are resolved; exact behavior when every nearby target already burns and duplicate-listener ownership need separate verification.
findings.resolutionDescription: Sunfire now keeps each copy's two-second application clock and prioritizes living unburned nearby targets using the declared abstract distance order. The combat-start application, per-copy listener ownership and nearest-target fallback when all eligible targets burn are retained explicit policies rather than newly verified native behavior.

findings.summary: Gunblade ally healing includes damage excluded by its native source filter.
findings.expected: Its native listener requires Damage.Source.Unit. Ionic Spark is Damage.Source.Item.IonicSpark and must not trigger this ally heal.
findings.observed: The engine heals allies from every credited damage packet. A Spark-only15-damage cast produces3 ally-heal potential, expected0.
limits: The standalone carry leaderboard does not simulate the ally health pool, so this changes reported support potential or team fights, not the protected holder's direct damage score.
findings.resolutionDescription: Gunblade ally healing now requires credited Unit-sourced damage. Item-sourced Spark and burn, and Trait damage, cannot grant ally healing. Native Unit-sourced Bramble remains eligible; self-omnivamp and the declared postdeath healing option remain separate policies.

findings.summary: The item note still says two tank dummies and a third non-tank.
findings.observed: The active benchmark contains four Tank-role frontliners and two non-tanks. The engine correctly applies its tank gate to all four configured tanks.
findings.resolutionDescription: The displayed Giant Slayer note now describes all four configured Tank-role frontliners and its Unit-source gate. This resolves the stale three-target wording without changing the benchmark formation.

history.note: The original finding observations, examples, probes, code/evidence references and detailed cache reports remain below as historical evidence from this engine. Their observed values are not claims about the corrected model. Original finding and matrix statuses are retained in originalStatus.

modelPolicy.damageIdentity: Unit, Item and Trait source identity is separate from attack/spell applicability. Native Bramble is Unit-sourced and untagged; source-only listeners retain it while Red and Titan applicability filters exclude it.
modelPolicy.periodicDamage: Quarter-second integration is retained, while item listeners and incoming-stack opportunities use separately bound native periods. Unknown native schedules do not invent extra gameplay hit, stack or critical-proc opportunities. Compound same-source terms settle as one logical hit.
modelPolicy.sunfire: Apply at combat start and each configured two-second deadline per copy; use the declared abstract distance order to prefer unburned nearby targets, with nearest-target fallback when all eligible targets burn. Start phase, duplicate ownership and fallback remain explicit policies.
modelPolicy.edgeCleanse: Clear supported transient combat debuffs, preserve permanent standalone benchmark assumptions, and resume overdue actor work at the current time without rewinding its clock.
modelPolicy.manaAndCrit: Keep existing native-consumer limits for mana locks and launch crit correlation; Nashor bonuses require accepted attack-tagged crits. Scuttle inherits attack applicability but retains its existing Precision damage gate until the shared crit-result producer is established.
